slides.texte_overlay:
How to get to know
your neighbours again
Say hello every time. In the hallway, the lift, the street. A simple greeting is how every neighbourly relationship starts.
Learn their names. Ask once, then use it. "Morning, Paul." Names turn strangers into people you know. Remember them.
Offer small help. Carry shopping up the stairs, take in a parcel, lend a tool. Small favours build trust quickly.
Invite them for a drink or coffee. A short, easy invitation. Many people are waiting for someone else to make the first move.
Before: I didn't know anyone on my street. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I always have something to chat about.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I didn't know anyone on my street. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I always have something to chat about.

slides.texte_overlay: Join local events. Street parties, markets, a local sports team. Being part of your area makes it feel like home.
Be considerate. Keep noise down at night and keep shared spaces clean. Good neighbours notice and do the same.
